Some of the ways that we form moral beliefs are unreliable, so a lot of our moral beliefs we shouldn't have that high credence in them.
There's a phenomenal introspection which involves reflecting on what our mental states are like is fairly reliable. He argued that it's regarded by evolutionary biologists and such to be reliable and informs us generally of the desirability of well-being. So when we're set on fire, we have the belief that it's bad that we were set on fire. And so I think that that's one way of getting around the evolutionary debunking arguments. I think.
I think that there are a variety of other ways. I think that whether evolutionary debunking arguments end up working is an empirical question. But again, the intuitions are just one line of evidence that I've provided. And for any line of evidence, it's always possible to, you know, it's possible for, you know, to explain any phenomena in alternative ways.
